articles.author: mara-voss
articles.title: Petalburg keeps the ball when Rustboro needs it back
articles.dek: Two fourth-quarter touchdowns, two successful two-point tries and six third-down conversions send the Pride through, 29–23.

body.text: Rustboro had a five-point lead with 2:29 remaining and an offense that had not punted all afternoon. Petalburg still had the ball to come, which turned out to be the more consequential possession. Iron Valiant led the Pride back into the end zone, Glalie completed a second successful two-point conversion, and the defense forced three straight incompletions on Rustboro’s next series. Petalburg won 29–23 and will visit Sunyshore.

I want to begin with the third downs because the late touchdown depends on them. Petalburg converted six of nine. Rustboro converted two of six. The Pride gained fewer total yards, 274 to 289, and did not force a turnover, yet they kept enough possessions alive to produce twenty-one fourth-quarter points. Their offense gave itself repeated opportunities to finish. Rustboro’s final meaningful drive lasted four snaps and ended on an incomplete fourth-and-nine pass.

The Stone’s running game was productive. My Way, Son gained seventy yards and scored on eleven carries; Philly Gabite added sixty-three on twelve. Shawn Watzon threw two touchdowns without an interception. Those facts make the defeat more difficult to explain with a simple bad-offense label. Rustboro had offensive answers. It needed one more sustained answer after Petalburg took the lead, and that was when the passing game stopped connecting.
The last touchdown required two difficult conversions

body.speaker: Norman
body.text: We needed the conversion before we could think about the touchdown. Glameow made that catch, then Magneton finished the next third down. We have to take the same care into the next game and make the earlier defensive possessions less difficult for ourselves.

My Way, Son’s five-yard touchdown run to the right put Rustboro ahead 23–18 at 2:29. The attempted two-point pass afterward failed, leaving Petalburg able to move ahead with a touchdown. Iron Valiant then worked through a possession that included a ten-yard completion to Venomoth, a nine-yard completion to Seviper and a short run by Whiscash. The Pride reached third-and-eight after an incompletion intended for Magneton.

At 1:26, Iron Valiant threw short right to Glameow for fourteen yards. That conversion brought Petalburg to the Rustboro 4. Two incompletions followed, first toward Glameow and then Vikavolt. On third-and-four, Iron Valiant found Magneton short left for the touchdown at 1:10. Glalie ran up the middle for the successful two-point try, and the Pride led 26–23 with 1:08 remaining.

Glameow finished with one catch for fourteen yards. Magneton finished with one catch for four yards. Both catches belonged to that final touchdown drive, and each answered a third down that could have left the Pride facing a much harder decision. A receiving leaderboard ordered by yardage would put them well below several teammates. The sequence explains why their contributions deserve prominent space in the game report.

Rustboro began its reply at its own 21 after Gengar’s seventeen-yard return. Philly Gabite gained one yard. Watzon then missed a short pass toward Gabite, had a deep throw toward Sudowoodo broken up by Rampardos, and missed Gengar on fourth-and-nine. Petalburg took over with fifty-five seconds left. Three Glalie runs used time and Rustboro’s remaining opportunities to stop it before Sunflora made a thirty-seven-yard field goal at 0:10.

body.alt: Glalie #95. Glalie converted the two-point try after Petalburg’s go-ahead touchdown. Editorial illustration.
body.caption: Glalie converted the two-point try after Petalburg’s go-ahead touchdown. Editorial illustration.

body.text: The final squib kick left Rustboro with four seconds. A one-yard run ended the afternoon. The decisive stop had already happened on the preceding possession, when the Pride defended three passes after allowing only one yard on first down. There was no late interception to decorate it. Petalburg simply denied the conversion that Rustboro needed to keep its season going.
A divisional game that stayed close

Iron Valiant opened the scoring with a one-yard touchdown pass to Seviper late in the first quarter. Rustboro answered almost immediately through its biggest passing play: Watzon found Gibby Timmy deep left for a forty-six-yard touchdown with six seconds left in the quarter. Both kickers made their first extra points. The teams traded field goals in the second quarter and entered halftime tied 10–10.

Petalburg’s Sunflora made a forty-eight-yarder at 3:21. Rustboro’s Gorebyss answered from thirty-nine yards at 0:52. The Pride’s Parasect had sacked Watzon for six yards during that Rustboro possession, the only sack recorded by either team. That pressure mattered without wrecking the entire drive; the Stone still came away with points. A close game often contains useful defensive plays that limit a possession rather than ending it outright.

Watzon found Geodude for a five-yard touchdown in the third quarter, moving Rustboro ahead 17–10 after the extra point. Petalburg replied early in the fourth with Glalie’s four-yard run up the middle. Iron Valiant then ran left for the two-point conversion, putting the Pride in front 18–17. My Way, Son’s touchdown restored Rustboro’s lead, setting up the final Petalburg scoring drive.

Those conversion decisions changed the score progression. Petalburg succeeded on both of its two-point tries and earned four points from them. Rustboro made its two conventional extra points and failed on the try following its third touchdown. The final margin was six, but the additional conversion points had already affected what each team needed on its subsequent possession. Petalburg’s second touchdown of the fourth quarter created a three-point lead rather than a one-point one.
Useful offense can still leave a team short

Watzon completed ten of sixteen passes for 126 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions. Gibby Timmy caught both of his targets for fifty-five yards; Geodude caught all four of his for thirty-three. Rustboro gained 163 rushing yards on twenty-seven carries and finished without a punt. The Stone also committed no recorded turnovers. This was a game lost despite several forms of offensive efficiency, which makes the defensive inability to finish third downs especially costly.

Petalburg’s quarterback completed seventeen of thirty for 141 yards and two touchdowns, adding thirty-nine rushing yards on five attempts. Glalie carried fourteen times for sixty-four yards and a score. Whiscash supplied thirty yards on five carries. The Pride generated seventeen first downs and ran fifty-four plays. They did not need a long touchdown to produce the winning drive; they needed several short completions, two difficult third-down answers and a final finish near the goal line.

body.alt: Porygon-Z #37. Shawn Watzon’s season ended in a six-point playoff loss. Imagined postgame scene.
body.caption: Shawn Watzon’s season ended in a six-point playoff loss. Imagined postgame scene.

body.text: Tyler Scarboro will have a specific defensive sequence to study rather than a general complaint about effort. Glameow gained fourteen on third-and-eight. Magneton scored on third-and-four after consecutive incompletions. Both plays came on the possession that changed the winner. The record does not reveal a private coverage call or assign blame to a particular defender, so the responsible diagnosis stops at the observed failure to secure those downs.

The same standard applies to Rustboro’s last possession. Three incompletions are enough to describe the result. They do not justify inventing a dropped pass, a missed read or a receiver running the wrong route. Rampardos’s breakup on the third-down throw is recorded and deserves credit. The other failures remain incomplete passes in the evidence available to readers.
Sunyshore will demand another complete finish

Petalburg entered the playoffs as a 12–5 division winner with a negative regular-season point differential. That combination invited skepticism, including fair questions about the Pride’s ability to score against strong opposition. Their wild-card win supplies a concrete response: twenty-nine points, a decisive fourth-quarter drive and a defensive stop when a rival needed one more possession. It does not erase the earlier season, but it earns the next game on its own terms.

Sunyshore just held Hearthome to six points and nineteen rushing yards. Petalburg will have to sustain its offense against a defense arriving with a much stronger recent performance than Rustboro’s third-down record. Oinkologne remains listed with one week of recovery, and Glalie’s new minor entry carries no remaining absence. Neither line should be turned into an invented lineup announcement. The Pride’s confirmed contributors have already shown what they can do in a close elimination game.

Rustboro finishes with a narrow defeat after a 9–8 regular season. Its running production and two clean touchdown throws made advancement possible; its inability to get the last needed stop, then the last needed conversion, decided the outcome. Petalburg travels on with the players who made those moments work. Glameow and Magneton will not lead the week’s yardage tables, but Sunyshore would be sensible to watch their third-down catches closely.

articles.author: rowan-vale
articles.title: Saffron turns a 10–7 deficit into thirty-five unanswered points
articles.dek: Archam Manning throws three touchdowns, Dam Skattebo runs for two, and Jack Slampert supplies the defensive finish in a 42–10 win.

body.text: Olivine led Saffron 10–7 in the second quarter. This is worth preserving because the final score, 42–10, is large enough to encourage everyone to misremember the first part. The Ironclads had intercepted Archam Manning and converted the resulting opportunity into a touchdown. Saffron then scored the next thirty-five points. The suspense lasted longer than the scoreboard now suggests, and substantially less long than Olivine needed.

Manning threw for 266 yards and three touchdowns. HeeDee Lamb caught six passes for 143 yards. Dam Skattebo ran for ninety-four yards and two scores. Jack Slampert returned an interception twenty yards for a touchdown. The Psi Corps advance to host Lavender, which has made late escapes a specialty and will now encounter a team that spent the second half making an escape unnecessary.

I have been accused of liking Saffron too much. I will allow the prosecution to use my previous columns. For this game, however, the evidence is unusually cooperative: 377 total yards to Olivine’s 181, three passing touchdowns, two rushing touchdowns and a second-half shutout. The most serious new concern is Emmitt Smoth’s five-week injury designation. Winning comfortably did not make the afternoon cost-free.
Olivine gave the favorite something to answer

body.speaker: Trent Scarboro
body.text: Emmitt helped us get here, and we are going to miss having him available. The players who are healthy have a job to carry forward. I loved the response after we fell behind, and I want that same commitment in the preparation for Lavender.

The Ironclads opened with a drive that ended in Sunflora’s forty-yard field goal at 3:37 of the first quarter. Mamoswine had begun that possession with an eighteen-yard run, and Drampa completed enough short passes to keep it moving despite a seven-yard sack by Chen Norton Jr. Olivine had three points and an early demonstration that it could reach scoring range.

Saffron replied with a fifty-two-yard touchdown drive. Manning found HeeDee Lamb for twenty-six yards deep left, then ten more on a short throw to the same side. Mothel Irving caught the three-yard touchdown pass short right at 2:09. The Psi Corps led 7–3. That opening answer used Lamb to move the offense and a different receiver to finish it, a pattern the Ironclads would struggle to contain throughout the game.

Manning’s first pass of the second quarter was intercepted by Olivine’s Ninetales and returned seventeen yards. The Ironclads used the resulting short field, with Bibarel scoring on a three-yard run up the middle at 4:08. Olivine led 10–7. It was a genuine opportunity for the seventh seed, earned through a defensive takeaway and a completed scoring possession.

The response came through two Saffron touchdown passes before halftime. Manning hit Lamb deep middle for twenty-two yards on third-and-four at 2:01. Later, facing third-and-two with ten seconds left, he found Bysson Witten short left for fourteen yards and another score. Saffron went to halftime ahead 21–10. The interception remained in Manning’s line, but it had not forced the offense into a cautious retreat.

body.alt: Heliolisk #11. HeeDee Lamb caught six passes for 143 yards. Editorial receiving illustration.
body.caption: HeeDee Lamb caught six passes for 143 yards. Editorial receiving illustration.

body.text: The third downs went to the passing game

Those two second-quarter touchdown throws were particularly damaging because Olivine had reached a down on which a stop would have changed the possession. Instead, Saffron scored from twenty-two and fourteen yards. The Psi Corps finished three of six on third down. Olivine finished three of twelve. The difference in conversion rate helped turn a brief underdog lead into a game with very few remaining possessions available for a comeback.

Manning completed seventeen of twenty-four attempts, with one interception and one sack taken. Lamb caught six of seven targets. Witten caught six of eight for sixty-three yards, and Mothel Irving added three catches for thirty-eight. Gengar Pickens supplied two catches for twenty-two yards. Saffron’s three touchdown passes went to three different receivers, preventing the Ironclads from reducing the scoring problem to one matchup.

Lamb’s longest catch gained forty-five yards, and his 143-yard total came on only six receptions. That production is why the headline receiving line belongs to him even though Witten matched his catch count. Both contributions mattered: one created large gains, the other repeatedly gave Manning a completion and finished the half with a touchdown. Their combined twelve catches accounted for most of the passing game’s successful attempts.

The new injury entries require a careful distinction. Lamb and Pach Tatum have minor entries with zero weeks remaining. Emmitt Smoth is listed for five weeks. The first two entries do not support an invented absence; the third is a substantial availability loss for the next round. Smoth had two carries for fourteen yards before the game ended, and the evidence does not timestamp the injury within a specific play.
Skattebo and Slampert close the game

Dam Skattebo scored on a fourteen-yard run up the middle at 4:18 of the third quarter. His second touchdown came on a ten-yard run to the right at 4:13 of the fourth. Those scores extended Saffron’s lead to 35–10. The Darmanitan finished with thirteen carries for ninety-four yards, averaging more than seven yards per attempt, and supplied the rushing work that allowed the offense to keep scoring after halftime.

Olivine’s following possession began with NeMarcus Tare sacking Drampa for six yards. On third-and-thirteen, Drampa’s short throw right was intercepted by Jack Slampert, who returned it twenty yards for a touchdown at 3:47. The score reached 42–10 after the extra point. Slampert finished with six tackles, the interception and the defensive touchdown, earning the game’s defensive-player honor.

That sequence put a defensive conclusion on an offensive win. Saffron had already established a comfortable lead, but the sack and interception prevented Olivine from using the remaining time to produce even a modest second-half response. Chen Norton Jr. added another seven-yard sack on the next Ironclads possession. He finished with two sacks; Tare had one. The pressure was productive without requiring a claim that every Olivine passing failure came from the same cause.

body.alt: Darmanitan #22. Dam Skattebo rushed for ninety-four yards and two touchdowns. Editorial rushing illustration.
body.caption: Dam Skattebo rushed for ninety-four yards and two touchdowns. Editorial rushing illustration.

body.text: Olivine’s final extended attempt ended on fourth-and-seven when Drampa completed a six-yard pass to Carnivine. Furfrou made the tackle. Saffron then ran twice with Skattebo and finished with Manning’s kneel. The final stop was one yard short of the conversion, an appropriately exact ending for a defense that had repeatedly made the Ironclads work through unhelpful down-and-distance situations.
Olivine’s season ends with a limited passing answer

Drampa completed fourteen of twenty-five passes for 118 yards, no touchdowns and one interception. Mamoswine led the rushing attack with sixty-six yards on eleven carries, but the rest of the ground production was much less effective. Olivine finished with sixty-three rushing yards overall after negative quarterback yardage and several short gains. Bibarel’s touchdown was valuable; his six carries produced six yards.

Delcatty led the receivers with forty-seven yards on three catches. Veluza added twenty-three, Mamoswine eighteen and Quilladin eleven. The Ironclads had one long Delcatty catch of thirty-four yards, but they did not produce enough sustained passing offense to keep pace after Saffron’s second-quarter answer. Nine first downs and four punts left them with a shrinking set of ways to recover the score.

Olivine entered as a 9–8 wild card and briefly led one of the conference’s strongest teams. That early work belongs in its account alongside the defeat. The full season review can wait for the offseason issue; this game ended because Saffron repeatedly scored touchdowns while the Ironclads stopped scoring altogether. No elaborate explanation is required to make a thirty-five-point unanswered run consequential.

Lavender now brings its return game, its late-possession nerve and its nine-game winning streak to Saffron. Trent Scarboro’s team has a clear advantage to build on: several different players just turned useful possessions into touchdowns. It also has a clear task after Smoth’s injury: preserve the backfield’s effectiveness with the healthy players actually available. Forty-two points make a persuasive opening statement. The divisional round will test whether Saffron can repeat the underlying execution against a survivor with a much better recent record.

art.alt: Swampert #99. Jack Slampert returned an interception twenty yards for a touchdown. Editorial illustration of the recorded return.
